previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with stage IV cholangiocarcinoma and biliary stents, was admitted with fever, chills, and elevated bilirubin. Imaging showed stent obstruction with sludge and pus, leading to cholangitis. He underwent an ERCP where both stents were cleared, and a new plastic stent was placed. His liver function improved, fevers resolved, and he was switched to oral antibiotics. Chemotherapy was held during admission and rescheduled. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans for stent removal in six weeks and resumed oncology care.

HISTORY:  ___ male with cholangiocarcinoma on chemotherapy, with
fevers and chills.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  Frontal and lateral views of the chest.  Biapical scarring is again
noted.  Calcification is seen in the right mid lung laterally.  Left basilar
linear opacities suggestive of atelectasis versus scarring.  The lungs are
otherwise clear.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette is within normal limits.  No
acute osseous abnormality is identified.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary process.

INDICATION:  ___ male with cholangiocarcinoma and recurrent fevers.

COMPARISON:  Chest CT, ___, CT abdomen and pelvis, ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial MDCT images were obtained through the chest after the
administration of IV contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformats were also
examined.

DLP:  338.70 mGy-cm. CTDIvol:  9.71 mGy.

FINDINGS:  The thyroid gland is unremarkable.  There is no mediastinal, hilar,
axillary or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.  The aorta and supra-aortic
branch vessels are unremarkable.  The main pulmonary artery is normal in
caliber.  The heart is unremarkable without pericardial effusion.

The central airways remain patent.  There is no new concerning lung nodule or
mass.  Again noted is a 1.1 cm calcified granuloma in the right upper lobe,
unchanged since the prior study.  There is no focal consolidation concerning
for pneumonia.  Plate-like atelectasis is noted at the lung bases bilaterally,
new since the prior study. There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

Left and right biliary stents are noted, as well as a smaller stent within the
left biliary stent.  Two fiducial markers are also present in the liver. 
Pneumobilia is expected and again seen.  Atrophy and heterogeneity of the left
lobe of the liver is unchanged. A small metallic marker is again noted along
the lesser curvature of the stomach. Several punctate splenic granulomas are
noted. These findings are better assessed on the recent CT abdomen and pelvis
from ___.  

No suspicious lesion is seen in visualized osseous structures.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No evidence of intrathoracic infection.  Bibasilar plate-like atelectasis.
2.  No new evidence of intrathoracic malignancy.
3.  Please see the recent CT abdomen and pelvis report for full discussion of
findings in the upper abdomen.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with cholangiocarcinoma, E coli bacteremia. got
PICC line but malpositioned. requesting repositioning.

COMPARISON:  CHEST X-RAY IN ___.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ (interventional radiology fellow) and
Dr. ___ (interventional radiology attending) performed the procedure.
The attending was present and supervising throughout the procedure.

ANESTHESIA:  No anesthesia required for today's case.

CONTRAST: 0 ml of Optiray contrast.

FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  1 min, Apx.  The 15mGy

PROCEDURE:  1. Repositioning of left PICC.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:

Initial fluoroscopic image demonstrated left-sided PICC line terminating in
the axilla. The left upper extremity was then prepped and draped in usual
sterile fashion.

A Nitinol wire was advanced through the existing PICC line into the superior
vena cava. The old PICC line was removed and a peel-away sheath was then
placed over a guidewire. A single lumen PIC line measuring 45 cm in length was
then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in the  SVC
under fluoroscopic guidance. Position of the catheter was confirmed by a
fluoroscopic spot film of the chest. The peel-away sheath and guidewire were
then removed.

The catheter was secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.

FINDINGS: 

Existing right arm approach PICC with tip in the left axilla.  Old PICC line
removed and replaced with a new single lumen PICC line with tip in the SVC.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful placement of a 45 cm left arm approach single lumen PICC with tip
in the SVC. The line is ready to use.
